title: The bridge test: can you hold a one-leg bridge for 20 seconds?
caption: Single leg glute bridge test: lift one foot, lift your hips and count how long you hold each side. Then do your level every day, from Glute Bridge up to Single-Leg Elevated Bridge, and test again in two weeks. Save this and retest.

overlays.text: Can you hold a one-leg bridge for 20 seconds? Try it, then swipe.

scenes.footer: Stop the count when your hips dip. Write down both sides.

overlays.text: On your back, one foot down, other knee up. Lift your hips. Count the seconds each side.

scenes.footer: Do this every day. Move on when all 10 feel easy.

overlays.text: Start here. Glute Bridge. 10 reps. Both feet down, push your hips up, lower slowly.

scenes.footer: Move on when every pause feels steady.

overlays.text: Paused Glute Bridge. 8 reps. Hips up, hold for three seconds, lower slowly.

scenes.footer: Move on when both sides stay level for all 8.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Glute Bridge. 8 each side. One foot down, other knee up, lift and lower.

scenes.footer: You passed. Brace the chair against a wall first.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Elevated Bridge. 6 each side. One heel on a chair, lift your hips.

scenes.footer: Same floor, same count. Write down both sides.

overlays.text: Do your level every day. Take the bridge test again in two weeks.

scenes.footer: Save this and retest in two weeks.

overlays.text: How many seconds, left and right?
